question: What are the recent research advancements in enhancing fluorescence for imaging?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that plasmonic nanoantennas produce highly enhanced local electromagnetic fields when pumped resonantly, addressing the size mismatch between light and nanoscale objects like single molecules, and thereby enhancing light-molecule interactions.
examples: Resonant pumping of plasmonic antennas concentrates optical fields
The light-molecule size mismatch motivates controlling light-molecule interactions

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer reports that lithographically fabricated gold bowtie nanoantennas achieve single-molecule fluorescence enhancements up to a factor of ~1,340, roughly ten times higher than previously reported.
examples: Enhancements up to a factor of 1,340 were observed with gold bowties
A tenfold improvement over earlier sharp-tip and colloid approaches

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer attributes the enhancement to greatly enhanced absorption and an increased radiative emission rate, raising the intrinsic quantum efficiency ~9× despite additional non-radiative ohmic losses.
examples: Enhanced absorption and increased radiative emission rate boost quantum efficiency
Simulations show ohmic losses are outweighed by radiative rate enhancement

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes film-coupled metal nanocube systems with emitters in the dielectric gap achieving spontaneous emission rate enhancements exceeding 1,000 (the largest observed) while maintaining high quantum efficiency (>0.5), directional emission (84% collection efficiency), and room-temperature operation.
examples: Film-coupled nanocubes show >1,000× Purcell enhancement with quantum efficiency above 0.5
Nanocube-over-gap geometry yields 84% collection efficiency directional emission

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer covers quantum-dot-based advances including multi-color and 3D single-particle tracking, in vivo tracking at molecular resolution in whole animals, and multiplexed QD immunohistochemistry enabling quantitative protein analysis in tissue samples.
examples: Multi-color and 3D QD tracking revealed cell signaling and protein trafficking mechanisms
Multiplexed QD IHC assays quantify proteins in tissue samples

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that dipole emitter orientation in nanogaps is vital to enhancement, that controlling all decay channels is required for practical devices, and that angle-resolved fluorescence measurements plus full-wave simulations were used to determine dipole orientations and predict time-resolved emission.
examples: Dipole orientation in the nanogap strongly affects enhancement
Angle-resolved measurements independently determined emission dipole orientations

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer acknowledges that lithographically fabricated antennas are more controllable and integration-friendly than sharp tips or colloids, and notes limitations such as non-radiative ohmic losses in metals that can quench fluorescence and the dependence of resonance on nanostructure size, shape, and material.
examples: Bowties offer a controllable, integrable structure compared to tips and colloids
Intrinsic metal losses cause non-radiative decay and quenching

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer distinguishes that plasmonic pumping readily increases Raman scattering, but whether fluorescence enhancement occurs depends on competing radiative and non-radiative rate factors.
examples: Fluorescence enhancement is not guaranteed by local field enhancement
Unlike Raman, fluorescence enhancement depends on competing radiative and non-radiative rates

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer connects these advances to applications such as high-contrast selection of single nanoemitters, nanophotonic lasers and single-photon sources, correlative light and electron microscopy, super-resolution imaging with QDs, and quantitative understanding of biological and disease processes.
examples: Nanoantennas enable high-contrast selection of single emitters
Upcoming QD applications include CLEM and super-resolution
